text:
Ottawa won a game that Toronto's own shot volume said was close, and the third period is where it stopped being close. The Senators out-chanced the Maple Leafs 2.79 to 0.99 in expected goals over the final 20 minutes, and the 89% look William Eklund got was the best chance of the night, only for Sergei Bobrovsky to stop it. Stephen Halliday's snap shot at 9:46, on a 7% chance, put OTT up 3-2 and ended the scoring.

The first two periods were even by expected goals. Thomas Chabot opened it at 18:51 of the first on a 5% wrist shot, the least likely goal of the game. Auston Matthews tied it 33 seconds into the second with a tip-in, and Kirill Marchenko put TOR ahead on a power-play backhand at 7:06. Michael Amadio levelled it at 12:40 on a 35% look from Tim Stützle and Chabot. TOR went 1 for 4 on the power play and OTT went 0 for 4, though OTT's four chances carried 1.55 expected goals to TOR's 0.85.

Over 60 minutes, OTT led 4.74 to 3.17 in expected goals, which works out to Ottawa deserving the win in 74% of simulated replays, even though TOR had 68 shot attempts to OTT's 54. Both teams put 29 shots on goal, so Bobrovsky (26 saves) and Linus Ullmark (27 saves) were busy equally. Both beat their expected numbers, Bobrovsky by 1.74 goals and Ullmark by 1.17. Chabot, the first star, logged 27:06 and was on the ice for 1.99 expected goals for against 1.14 against. Claude Giroux added two assists.
